name: Dendi Kingdom (Songhai successor)
summary: The Songhai who refused Moroccan rule after 1591 held out downriver on the Niger in the Dendi kingdom, until French conquest around 1900.

location.value: The easternmost Songhai province; modern centres are Gaya (Niger), Kamba (Nigeria) and Malanville (Benin).

terrain.value: The Niger river valley and open savanna.

climate.value: A Sahel climate with a short rainy season.

disasters.value: Droughts and floods along the Niger affected harvests.

urbanisation.value: Mostly villages; a royal or market town.

migration.value: Refugees fled to Dendi after the Songhai defeat; the article does not describe a southward movement.

economicBase.value: Farming, fishing and trade on the Niger.

tradeRoutes.value: Niger river trade linked the kingdom to the interior and the coast.

wealth.value: Modest, compared with the old Songhai Empire.

moneyAndTax.value: Tribute, cloth, cowries and trade goods.

inequality.value: Rulers and nobles above farmers; captives and slaves at the bottom.

governmentType.value: Governed by a Dendi-fari (governor of the eastern front); members of the Askia dynasty fled there after defeat by the Saadi dynasty of Morocco.

keyRulers.value: Askia Nuh (son of Askia Dawud; capital at Lulami; resisted Mahmud ibn Zarqun for two years; deposed in 1599). No reign dates are given.

succession.value: The Askia family held the throne, and disputes were common.

institutions.value: A royal court with inherited offices.

stability.value: Increasingly unstable reigns, coups and counter-coups; smaller Songhai kingdoms emerged.

eliteConflict.value: Rival princes competed for the Askia throne.

majorWars.value: War with Morocco: Mahmud ibn Zarqun ended the war in 1594 and was killed that year; Mansur continued it until 1599.

territoryChange.value: Shrank to the Dendi region after the Moroccan conquest of Gao.

alliancesRivals.value: Moroccan pashas; in 1609 Djenné revolted with Songhai support; the Saadi later left the area to Tuareg and Fulbe nomads.

scienceEducation.value: Oral learning; Qur’anic schools where Islam spread.

openness.value: Open to trade along the Niger.

religion.value: Islam; the pre-Islamic bori cult almost completely disappeared by the mid-1950s.

languageWriting.value: Dendi Songhai dialect; Zarma is listed among the ethnic groups.

artsArchitecture.value: Mud-brick buildings in the Sudano-Sahelian style.

sharedIdentity.value: Loyalty to the ruler and lineage.

dailyLife.value: Village farming; cassava, millet or sorghum.

neighbours.value: Pashalik of Timbuktu, Borgu, Hausa states.

ideasReligions.value: Islam, practised by the rulers and many scholars.

colonisation.value: Survived as a kingdom until 1901, when France conquered it and incorporated it into French West Africa.

riseSignals.value: The Battle of Tondibi, where Askia forces were defeated by Morocco’s Saadi dynasty (the article gives no date).

declineSignals.value: Fragmentation into small chiefdoms, then French conquest.

outcome.value: Became part of French West Africa around 1900.

overallCertainty.value: Known from oral traditions, travellers and colonial records; many dates are approximate.
